content: Isopropyl acetate is an ester, which is an organic compound formed through the condensation reaction between acetic acid and isopropanol. It appears as a clear, colorless liquid and is characterized by a distinct fruity odor. This compound functions as a solvent with extensive applications in manufacturing processes. It is miscible with most organic solvents and exhibits moderate solubility in water. Isopropyl acetate is commonly employed as a solvent for cellulose, plastics, oils, and fats. Additionally, it is a constituent in certain printing inks and perfumes. When isopropyl acetate comes into contact with steel in the presence of air, it undergoes slow decomposition, yielding acetic acid and isopropanol as byproducts. It reacts violently with oxidizing agents and has a corrosive effect on many types of plastics.
